title: Appendix B — The Problem of the Intrinsic (as reflected in the Neo-Aristotelian School)
folder: Burke - The Problem of the Intrinsic
role: Second Appendix essay. Burke engages the Chicago Neo-Aristotelian school of literary criticism (R. S. Crane, Norman Maclean, Elder Olson, with Yvor Winters as adjacent figure) on the question of intrinsic versus extrinsic methods of critical analysis — whether a literary work's motive-content can be analyzed solely from internal textual evidence or whether contextual / biographical / ideational extrinsic considerations must enter. Burke clarifies that the intrinsic/extrinsic distinction (already developed as a substance vocabulary subsection in GM-02) is itself a scene-act ratio meta-question: what scope of scene does the critic admit, and what acts of the agent count as evidence? The essay is the volume's most explicit methodological meta-clarification of how the pentad apparatus relates to other critical schools.
